subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should maintainers sponsor a live Twilio/OpenAI realtime repro now, or wait for the reporter to provide a redacted audio sample, packet capture, or level/queue logs before changing the audio pipeline?
rationale: The current code path is clear, but source inspection cannot distinguish clipping from provider output, telephony pacing, backpressure, codec conversion, or carrier playback without live audio evidence.

options.title: Run live repro first
options.body: Use a maintainer-owned Twilio/OpenAI setup to capture redacted audio and level/queue diagnostics before choosing gain, codec, or pacing changes.

options.title: Wait for reporter artifact
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a redacted audio sample, packet capture, or output-level log before spending maintainer telephony time.

options.title: Close only after clean proof
options.body: Close this issue only if current main is proven clean on the reported outbound Twilio/OpenAI path or a targeted fix lands with live proof.

recommendation.title: Run live repro first
recommendation.body: Use a maintainer-owned Twilio/OpenAI setup to capture redacted audio and level/queue diagnostics before choosing gain, codec, or pacing changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision crosses shared codec behavior and live proof expectations, and steipete has recent history on the codec/test surface.
